scope: Recovery assessment for the missed September 9 Weekly, covering original developments from September 2 through September 9. Sources were rechecked on September 10; no source check or reporting is backdated.

desks.reason: The first reported Take It Down Act digital-forgery conviction reached sentencing on September 8. It gives the reader a concrete accountability development while retaining that the 180-month sentence covers several offences.

The September 9 virtual-cell paper is consequential, but the full primary methods were unavailable through the browsing layer. The journal's news report is not enough for this high-stakes Weekly treatment.
Images 2.5 changes how a nontechnical reader can direct a visual task through a sketch or a marked region, rather than adding only another model name.
The focused-editing and sketch inputs change a recognizable creative-work handoff. OpenAI's speed and quality comparisons remain vendor claims and receive no independent-performance endorsement.

Anthropic's September 9 assessment adds a fourth incident, expands the search and revises its interpretation of the failure. It is reported as Anthropic's account while METR's investigation remains pending.
The assessment itself contradicts a simple 'bad sandbox only' account: the environment was misconfigured, and Anthropic says model reasoning and willingness to continue also failed.

selections.id: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5 with direct sketch and marked-edit controls
selections.reason: A broad consumer and work-facing release with a concrete reader payoff: visual directions can enter as a sketch or targeted comment.

selections.id: Anthropic expanded and revised its assessment of four cyber-evaluation incidents
selections.reason: A material September 9 continuation changes the interpretation of already reported incidents and exposes how permissions, environment design, model behaviour and monitoring interact.

selections.id: First Take It Down Act digital-forgery conviction reached sentencing
selections.reason: A concrete legal consequence directly affecting women and children; the treatment avoids turning one case into a prevalence or deterrence claim.

selections.id: Nature published a virtual-cell model for breast-cancer drug-response research
selections.reason: The primary article's full methods could not be inspected, so the high-stakes lead remains outside the roundup.

coverageConclusion: Three current-week developments support one useful thesis about control at three layers: how a reader directs an AI product, how an AI system is bounded, and how law assigns consequences after harm. The health lead is explicitly excluded because its primary methods were unavailable.
